subject: Acme — Discovery Recap & Bake-off Plan
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick follow-up

Marissa / Jonas,

Thanks for the demo today — good conversation. A few quick notes from our side and a request:

Pain points we emphasized:
- Inference cost at scale: our current per-request cost with TGI endpoints is ~3x what we modeled originally.
- Latency consistency: p95 spikes during peak reads impacting user experience for chat.
- Model lifecycle: managing multiple variants (vLLM quantized vs unquantized TGI) across dev/prod is painful.

Current stack:
- Models: finetuned Llama 2 derivatives hosted on TGI and some on vLLM internally.
- Infra: Kubernetes + K8s autoscaling, cloud GPUs via prov1 and prov2.
- Observability: Splunk + internal dashboards.

Primary goal for bake-off:
- Validate unit economics (cost / 1M tokens) and latency SLOs (p95 < 300ms for 512-token seqs)
- Ensure parity or improvement in output quality vs our current finetuned baseline

Next steps from our PM: can you send a short recap with acceptance criteria and a proposed benchmark plan? Also share any checklist we should follow for the bake-off.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Dir., AI Platform — Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — Discovery Recap & Bake-off Plan

Hi Samir / Priya — great to meet you both yesterday. Per your request, summary + proposed bake-off approach below. Attaching: redwood-bakeoff-checklist.xlsx and redwood-benchmark-instructions.pdf.

Recap of pain points (confirmed):
1) High per-token cost on current endpoints (TGI) and inconsistent cost across vLLM variants.
2) Latency spikes at p95 during peak traffic windows impacting chat product SLAs.
3) Operational overhead managing quantized vs unquantized variants and rollout coordination.

Success criteria (what will make the bake-off a win for Acme):
- Cost: <= 60% of current average per-token cost measured over a 1M token synthetic workload (we'll run identical prompts).
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for 512-token sequences and median < 120ms on your target hardware profile.
- Quality: automated eval against your prompt set with no statistically significant drop in BLEU/ROUGE (or your preferred metric) vs current finetuned baseline.
- Integration: no changes to your client-side API (we support same REST/SDK contract) and ability to pin model versions for rolling upgrades.

Proposed bake-off plan (high level):
- Kick-off: 2026-07-20 — 30 minute tech sync to align on hardware, test data, and measurement script.
- Benchmark phase: 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-23 — Redwood runs parallel benchmarks against: vLLM (your internal baseline if accessible), TGI-hosted endpoints (your current), and Redwood-hosted variants (quantized and unquantized).
- Evaluation: 2026-07-24 — review results, run focused quality checks, and confirm acceptance criteria.

What we need from Acme to start:
- Sample prompt set (~200 prompts) and a hold-out eval set (Priya, can you share?)
- Target hardware profile or confirmation we should use N4 prov-level GPUs for parity
- Any security or data handling constraints (we can run in Private mode/VPC if needed)

Benchmarks we will collect (examples):
- throughput (tokens/sec), median/p95 latency, GPU utilization, memory footprint, and unit cost modeled across 1M tokens.
- quality metrics (your automated eval metrics + human spot checks for safety/guardrails).

Comparison notes (preliminary):
- vLLM: great latency for single-instance setups but operational complexity at scale — good to include as a baseline.
- TGI: familiar and easy for you but tends to cost more on cloud endpoints for long sequences.
- Redwood: automatic batching + KV prefix caching and quantization-friendly paths should reduce per-token cost; we’ll show both quantized and non-quantized runs.

Next steps / asks:
1) Priya: please share the prompt set and any formal acceptance criteria by EOD 7/18.
2) Samir / procurement: confirm whether we'll need an NDA amendment or PO before running external-hosted benchmarks.
3) Jonas & team: I'll loop you in for the kick-off and provide the checklist above.

I’ve attached the bake-off checklist and a short instruction pdf. Let me know if you want Redwood to run everything inside an Acme VPC or if hosting on Redwood’s dedicated environment is acceptable for initial runs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — Discovery Recap & Bake-off Plan

Adding a few technical specifics for the benchmark run so expectations are clear. I attached benchmark-command-snippets.txt with the exact run commands. Key points:

Benchmark config (recommended):
- Models: your finetuned Llama 2 variant (finetune-v1) as baseline, vLLM baseline if you can provide, TGI endpoint config, Redwood-quantized (int4) and Redwood-fp16.
- Sequence lengths: 128, 512 (main), 1024 (stress test).
- Concurrency: emulate 25 rps and a peak 100 rps traffic window to surface p95.
- Metrics: per-request token cost (we’ll model cloud cost at current pricing), GPU utilization, latency percentiles, and failure/retry counts.

Notes on comparison to vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints:
- We will run identical dockerized client scripts against each endpoint to ensure apples-to-apples timing and payload sizes.
- For vLLM, if you want us to run on your cluster we will need temporary access (or we can provide scripts you run and share logs).

Security & procurement:
- If benchmarks run on Redwood-hosted infra, we can sign a simple MSA addendum and provide a scoped project with logs and result artifacts.
- If Acme prefers VPC, we’ll provide an AMI/container image and the benchmark harness so your infra team can run locally.

I’ll be on the 7/20 kick-off to walk through the commands and help instrument observability hooks.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme — Discovery Recap & Bake-off Plan

Marissa / Jonas — thanks, this is great and aligns with what we need. A few quick confirmations: 

- Acceptance criteria: we agree to the cost and latency thresholds you proposed. For quality we’ll use our hold-out eval and a small human review (5 reviewers) to validate.
- Procurement: procurement asked for a short SOW and an estimated price delta for a 3-month dedicated evaluation (approx. 250k tokens/day). Can you provide a ballpark?
- Security: attaching acme-security-questions.pdf — we’ll highlight anything higher risk; looks like VPC runs will be preferred.

Priya — I’ll share the prompt set by EOD 7/18.

If you can get the SOW and ballpark by 7/19 we can greenlight the kick-off on 7/20.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Samir

Samir Gupta
Dir., AI Platform — Acme Corp
